spec: Google Benchmark (third-party: benchmark, benchmark_main) builds under its own unconditional -pedantic-errors with every clang 22.x, including apt clang 22.1.2 where -Wno-error=X does not downgrade -pedantic-errors diagnostics (that override only exists from clang 22.1.4, llvm-project #184756): the __COUNTER__ C2y-extension diagnostic is disabled outright (-Wno-c2y-extensions, added only when the compiler knows the flag) for those dependency targets, so their build emits no -Wc2y-extensions diagnostic at all; our own targets keep their warning set and -Werror

tests: clang 22 ci-release build of benchmark and benchmark_main emits no -Wc2y-extensions diagnostic
clang 22 ci-release build of benchmark and benchmark_main emits no -Wc2y-extensions diagnostic
events.command: sh -c 'cmake --build build/clang22-ci-release --target benchmark benchmark_main --clean-first > build/clang22-ci-release-bm.log 2>&1 || { tail -20 build/clang22-ci-release-bm.log; exit 2; }; if grep -n "Wc2y-extensions" build/clang22-ci-release-bm.log | head -6; then grep -m1 -oE "pedantic-errors.*-Wno-error=c2y-extensions" build/clang22-ci-release-bm.log; exit 1; fi; echo "benchmark/benchmark_main: no -Wc2y-extensions diagnostic"'
events.reason: Dependencies.cmake only adds -Wno-error=c2y-extensions to benchmark/benchmark_main, which merely downgrades the __COUNTER__ C2y-extension diagnostic (benchmark.h:1461) that Google Benchmark's unconditional -pedantic-errors turns into an error. The downgrade of a -pedantic-errors diagnostic by -Wno-error=X exists only from clang 22.1.4 (llvm-project 10be0a255205, #184756); apt clang 22.1.2 on ubuntu-26.04 keeps it an error (runs 45933415417 ci/ci-release and 45933415430 benchmark). Local Homebrew clang 22.1.7 shows the same root cause as the diagnostic still being emitted (as a warning) by the dependency build, so the build depends on that compiler-version-specific override instead of the diagnostic being disabled
